meta.subtitle: Subsea backlog is converting at higher margins, but at $68.82 the shares already sit near the consensus path

analystSentiment.commentary:
TechnipFMC's 10-Q for the three months ended June 30, 2026 shows revenue of $2,763.1 million, up 9.0% year over year, with the increase credited to Subsea backlog conversion. Net income rose faster than revenue, helped by lower net interest expense and a lower effective tax rate as well as by operations.

The operating record is strong: the vendor's operating margin rose in each year from FY21 to FY25, and net debt turned negative in FY24. The balance sheet is no longer a constraint.

The stock already reflects much of that. At $68.82 it trades at 24.0x trailing earnings and sits in the upper part of its 52-week range. The consensus target of $75.95 implies +10.4%, and our probability-weighted value lands below that. We rate the shares **HOLD** with a $65 to $80 target range; the scenario section carries the full argument.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
TechnipFMC plc designs, manufactures, installs and services equipment for offshore and onshore oil and natural gas developments, and was founded in 1884 and headquartered in Newcastle upon Tyne, per the company tearsheet. The tearsheet describes two segments, Subsea and Surface Technologies; the vendor data in this report treat the company as a single consolidated segment, so we do not quote a segment split.

FY25 revenue was $9.9B, up 9.4%, with FY25 diluted EPS of $2.30. Consensus expects revenue of ~$10.7B in FY26. The company also runs a New Energy business that the 10-Q says is executing carbon capture and emissions-reduction projects offshore Brazil and in the UK.

thesis.label: HOLD
thesis.body: The business case is sound: the vendor tables show five years of revenue growth, operating margin expansion and debt reduction, and the second quarter of 2026 extended the trend. The valuation case is thinner. The shares trade at 21.9x forward (NTM) earnings and 12.6x trailing EV/EBITDA, and the consensus target sits only modestly above the price. Our probability-weighted value is close to today's price, which supports **HOLD** rather than BUY. The counter-case to our caution is that offshore spending keeps rising through the decade, as management argues in the 10-Q, which would push earnings above consensus.

catalysts: Continued Subsea backlog conversion in the next 10-Q; the growth section covers the backlog evidence.
Awards in new offshore basins that the 10-Q names, such as Suriname and Mozambique.
Progress on New Energy projects, including Mero 3 HISEP for Petrobras.
A shift of operator capital toward offshore if Middle East risk is re-rated, which management describes as likely.
risks: A sustained fall in oil and gas spending, a risk factor in the 10-K filed 2026-02-19.
Losses on fixed-price contracts or late backlog delivery.
Valuation compression from a multiple already above its forward level.
Currency swings, which already raised foreign currency remeasurement losses in the second quarter of 2026.

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.incomeCommentary:
Revenue rose every year from $6.4B in FY21 to $9.9B in FY25, and operating margin rose every year from 2.9% to 14.5%. The trend held in 2026. Second-quarter revenue was $2,763.1 million against $2,534.7 million a year earlier, and gross profit rose to $684.7 million from $593.3 million.

The 10-Q credits the quarter's revenue gain to Subsea, whose revenue rose $270.6 million. That Subsea increase is larger than the consolidated increase, so the rest of the company's revenue declined year over year; the truncated 10-Q excerpt does not carry the Surface Technologies table that would show by how much. Subsea operating profit margin was 19.6% versus 17.2%.

Below the operating line, net income of $362.1 million was up 35.0%, faster than pre-tax income at 27.1%. Two non-operating items helped: net interest expense fell to $3.6 million from $14.4 million, and the effective tax rate fell to 24.0% from 28.4%, which the 10-Q attributes to the geographic distribution of earnings. Neither is a repeatable source of growth at the same pace, so we weight the pre-tax line.

The vendor's 19.0% operating margin for the quarter sits above what the 10-Q's revenue less total costs and expenses implies; we rely on the 10-Q's lines.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.balanceCommentary:
Total debt fell every year, from $2.0B in FY21 to $0.4B in FY25, and net debt moved from $0.7B to a net cash position of $0.6B over the same span. Trailing net debt/EBITDA is -0.3x and interest coverage is 25.9x, so leverage does not constrain the company.

The weaker line is liquidity. The current ratio slid from 1.39 in FY21 to 1.13 in FY25 and stands at 1.08 on a trailing basis, while cash and short-term investments ended FY25 at $1.0B, below the FY21 level. Total equity was roughly flat over five years. The data do not say why the current ratio declined; for a contractor that can reflect customer advances on projects, but the source does not confirm that, so we treat it as a point to watch rather than a problem.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.cashflowCommentary:
Free cash flow reached $1.4B in FY25, up from the FY24 level, on operating cash flow of $1.8B and capital expenditure that held at $0.3B. FCF margin was 14.6%, and the trailing FCF yield is 5.8%.

The series is not smooth. Free cash flow fell to $0.2B in FY22 before recovering, which shows how much project cash timing can move a single year. The vendor data do not explain the FY25 step-up, so we do not treat it as a run rate.

Shareholder returns are small relative to cash generation: the dividend yield is 0.29%, and the vendor's buyback line shows no data after FY21, which we read as missing rather than zero.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
The shares trade at 24.0x trailing earnings, 21.9x NTM earnings and ~19.0x FY27E earnings, with EV/EBITDA of 12.6x and P/S of 2.6x. No peer multiples were captured, so we cannot say whether these are rich or cheap against comparable contractors.

The forward multiples rest on consensus EPS of $3.14 for FY26E and $3.62 for FY27E. The consensus basis is not stated, and the trailing multiple rests on GAAP figures, so the step-down from trailing to forward multiples mixes bases and should not be read as purely GAAP.

The price of $68.82 sits well above the 52-week low of $35.29 and below the high of $80.70. The Street is constructive, with 14 Buy, 6 Hold and 1 Sell ratings, and a median target of $80.00. The multiple already credits most of the expected earnings growth.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Offshore capital keeps shifting toward deepwater, new-basin awards convert, and Subsea margins keep expanding, so earnings beat FY27E consensus of $3.62 and the market holds a premium multiple. We anchor to the Street-high target of $87.00 over 12 months.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: The company delivers roughly consensus EPS of $3.14 for FY26E, backlog converts on schedule, and the multiple holds near current levels as FY27E rolls into view. We anchor to the consensus target of $75.95 over 12 months.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Lower oil prices slow operator spending, some backlog is re-scheduled, and fixed-price execution slips, so earnings fall short of consensus and the multiple de-rates toward cyclical levels. We anchor to the Street-low target of $45.00 over 12 months.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
The three scenarios are alternative paths for offshore spending over 12 months, so they are either/or rather than additive. Base carries 55% because the second quarter of 2026 showed backlog converting on plan and consensus does not require margin gains beyond what the company is already reporting.

Bull carries 25%. Management's 10-Q argues that offshore activity will remain strong through the end of the decade, and a Middle East risk re-rating could pull capital offshore faster, but those are management views, not booked orders.

Bear carries 20%. The 10-K's demand risk factor ties demand to oil and gas spending and notes that declines can lead to cancellation or re-scheduling of backlog orders. In that path both earnings and the multiple fall together, which is why the Bear sits at the Street-low target rather than a modest discount.

The weighted fair value comes out a little above the current price and below the consensus target. That expected upside is too small to clear the BUY threshold, while the Bear downside is large, so the reward/risk is poor. That gives **HOLD**, with a $65 to $80 target range that brackets the Base.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body:
The vendor data report a single consolidated segment, with FY25 revenue of $9.9B. The company tearsheet and the 10-Q describe two operating segments, Subsea and Surface Technologies; we do not quote a revenue split between them.

The 10-Q shows Subsea driving recent growth, with second-quarter Subsea operating profit up 27.9%. The 10-Q says surface activities on US land were less than five percent of total Company revenue in 2025, so onshore North America is a small exposure. The investment case rests on Subsea, and Surface Technologies is a secondary contributor whose recent trend is not visible in the excerpt.

moatFactors.name: Integrated iEPCI model
moatFactors.body: The 10-Q says iEPCI combines subsea production systems, umbilicals, risers and flowlines, and installation vessels in one contract, and that it created a new market. Integrated scope raises switching costs once a client standardizes on it. The counter-case is the 10-K's risk factor on competition and ongoing industry consolidation, which could produce rivals with similar scope.

moatFactors.name: Subsea 2.0 configure-to-order
moatFactors.body: Management claims Subsea 2.0 delivers up to 25 percent lower product cost and as much as a 12-month reduction in delivery time for subsea production equipment. A cost and schedule edge of that kind would support pricing. These are company claims in the 10-Q, not independently verified figures.

moatFactors.name: Installed-base services
moatFactors.body: The 10-Q points to Subsea Services growing from an aging installed base. Service work on equipment the company installed tends to stay with the original supplier, but the excerpt gives no services revenue figure, so we cannot size it.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat NARROW. The operating margin expansion from FY21 to FY25 is consistent with an advantage in integrated offshore execution, but the business remains tied to operator spending cycles that it does not control, and the 10-K flags fixed-price contract losses as a risk. The advantage is real enough to protect returns during normal cycles, not strong enough to shield earnings from a sustained spending downturn.

points: Backlog was 17.4% higher at December 31, 2025 than a year earlier, according to the 10-Q, and its conversion drove 2026 revenue growth. Six-month revenue rose 10.2% to $5,255.8 million. The 10-Q excerpt does not give a backlog figure as of June 30, 2026, so we cannot tell whether orders are still outrunning revenue.

Subsea gross profit rose $104.8 million in the second quarter, of which $62.8 million came from volume and $42.1 million from favorable activity mix. Mix gains of that size can reverse as project phases change, so we do not extrapolate them.

New offshore basins add optionality: the 10-Q cites an iEPCI award for TotalEnergies' GranMorgu project in Suriname and participation in Eni's Coral North project in Mozambique. These are named projects, but the excerpt gives no values for them.

New Energy work includes the Mero 3 HISEP project for Petrobras and an all-electric subsea iEPCI for carbon capture and storage for the Northern Endurance Partnership. These broaden the addressable market, though the excerpt gives no revenue contribution.

Consensus expects revenue of $11.4B and EPS of $3.62 in FY27E. Delivering that requires growth to continue at roughly the recent pace, which the backlog supports for now but which depends on operator spending holding up.

management.leadership: No earnings call transcript or press release was captured, and the proxy excerpt carries no executive titles or tenures, so we judge leadership on execution. On that basis the record is good, as the financials section sets out. Management's 10-Q outlook is confident about offshore activity through the end of the decade; we treat that as a forecast rather than evidence. Higher share-based compensation drove a $27.8 million rise in six-month SG&A, which is a cost to watch.
management.capitalAllocation:
Capital went first to deleveraging, as the balance-sheet discussion shows. Capital expenditure has stayed low relative to cash generation, and the dividend is small.

The vendor's buyback line shows no data after FY21, so we cannot say how much stock was repurchased. The vendor's share count of ~392.16M, derived from market cap, sits below the 401,559,289 shares the proxy reports outstanding on March 1, 2026; the prompt carries no data that explains the gap. The 10-K also notes that as an English public limited company, TechnipFMC must meet additional financial requirements before it may declare dividends or repurchase shares. With net cash on the balance sheet, how management deploys free cash flow is the open question.
management.governance:
Governance facts come from the proxy statement dated 2026-03-19. The NomGov Committee reviews director independence annually under NYSE and SEC standards. The Board has no tenure limit and states that the average tenure of independent directors will be approximately seven years if all nominees are elected.

The Board considered that three directors served at companies with ordinary-course commercial relationships with the Company in 2025, and that one director sits on the board of FMC Corporation, the former parent, with which the Company has separation and joint litigation defense agreements dating from the 2001 separation. The Board concluded none of these affected independence. The related-person review covers transactions above $120,000. We see nothing in the excerpt that weakens outside holders' position.
management.insiderOwnership:
As of March 1, 2026, all current directors, executive officers and NEOs as a group held 5,749,283 shares, or 1.4% of the class, per the 2026 proxy. Douglas J. Pferdehirt held 3,921,924 shares, including 970,547 shares under options exercisable within 60 days. Insiders have meaningful personal exposure but no control.

The proxy lists four holders above 5%: The Vanguard Group at 9.94%, BlackRock, Inc. at 9.33%, T. Rowe Price Associates, Inc. at 9.04% and T. Rowe Price Investment Management, Inc. at 5.54%. These figures come from the holders' own Schedule 13G or 13D filings, and the Vanguard figure rests on a filing dated February 13, 2024, so it is stale. No holder is near a controlling stake; ownership is dispersed among index and active managers, which leaves outside holders' votes decisive.

idiosyncratic: Fixed-price contracts: the 10-K warns the company may lose money on fixed-price contracts. A cost overrun on a large iEPCI project would hit margins directly. Watch for charges or margin reversals in Subsea operating profit in coming quarters.

Backlog delivery: the 10-K says failure to deliver backlog on time could affect future sales, profitability and customer relationships. Watch the pace of revenue conversion against backlog in the next 10-Q.

Reliance on subcontractors, suppliers and joint venture partners, per the 10-K: a partner failure on an integrated project lands on the company's own schedule and cost. Watch for restructuring or impairment charges, which were $5.0 million in the second quarter of 2026.

Competition and industry consolidation, a separate 10-K risk factor: a consolidated rival with integrated scope could compete on price. Watch for pressure on Subsea margins without a matching fall in volume.
risks.systemic: The 10-K's demand risk factor ties demand to oil and natural gas activity and capital spending, which in turn follow volatile commodity prices; a sustained decline can lead to cancellation, modification or re-scheduling of backlog orders. The same section lists geopolitical conflicts, such as unrest in the Middle East, among factors that move prices. The 10-Q adds that the Middle East conflict could re-rate regional risk in a way management expects to favor offshore, so the geopolitical effect cuts both ways. Currency is a second channel: other expense rose $8.0 million in the second quarter of 2026, mainly from foreign currency remeasurement losses. Watch oil prices, operator capital budgets and new order announcements.

body: We rate TechnipFMC **HOLD** with a $65 to $80 target range. The business is executing well and the balance sheet carries net cash, but the price already reflects most of the consensus earnings path, and the downside in a spending downturn outweighs the upside. We would turn more constructive on a lower entry price or on evidence that earnings are running ahead of consensus, such as a backlog update showing orders still outpacing revenue.
